newsitem.title: BULGARIA: STAKE IN BULBANK TO PAY FOR BULGARIAN BANK BAIL.
newsitem.headline: STAKE IN BULBANK TO PAY FOR BULGARIAN BANK BAIL.

text.p: A stake in Bulgaria's biggest state-owned Bulbank may be offered for privatisation as a funding source for $50 million stabilisation programme for Biochimbank, the State Gazette said on Friday.

"Proceeds from sales of stakes in Bulbank and the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company, whichever comes first, will cover at a priority the T-note issue to be placed with Bulbank under the stabilisation plan for Biochimbank," the State Gazette said.

Under the government decree the Finance ministry would place $50 million of T-notes with Bulbank to fund the purchase of $50 million of dollar-denominated bad debt bonds at par value from the ailing state-owned Biochimbank's portfolio.
The ministry would then write off the par value of the bad debt bonds from the state debt.
The minimum acceptable price of dollar-denominated bad debt (ZUNK) bonds issued in 1994 is now set at 45 percent of par.
The T-note issue to be placed with Bulbank has a 18-month maturity and a semi-annual coupon pegged to the six-month LIBOR.

In line with the memorandum of economic policies agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) last month the government has announced that Bulgaria was ready to sell a majority stake in its telecommunication company.
Under the accord with the IMF Bulgaria has also pledged to privatise all of its six operational state-owned banks by the end of 1998.

So far Bulgaria has offered a 35 percent stake in the United Bulgarian Bank to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) but not specified what stakes in the five other banks it was ready to offer for sale.

Bulbank's assets amounted to 1.349 trillion levs ($2.77 billion) which compared only to the Bulgarian National Bank's (BNB) assets of 1.255 trillion levs ($2.57 billion) at the end of 1996, BNB and Bulbank balance figures showed.
The Bank Consolidation Company (BCC), which manages state equity in local commercial bank holds 98.03 percent of Bulbank.

Last year the Bulbank posted 12.4 billion levs net-profit after setting aside provisions against risk assets of 163.9 billion levs and paying 9.6 billion levs of taxes on a gross profit of 185.7 billion levs. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
